entrance_direction.label: Main entrance
entrance_direction.rationale: The main entrance is traditionally treated as the primary point through which energy enters the home.

remedies.structural: Where practical, consult a qualified architect before changing the entrance position or door opening.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the entrance bright, uncluttered, clearly marked and in good repair.

kitchen_direction.label: Kitchen
kitchen_direction.rationale: Traditional Vastu associates the kitchen with the fire element and favours the South-East sector.

remedies.structural: During renovation, consider locating the primary cooking zone toward South-East where feasible.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the cooking area clean and well ventilated; place the hob so the cook can preferably face East when practical.

master_bedroom_direction.label: Master bedroom
master_bedroom_direction.rationale: The South-West is traditionally associated with stability and is often preferred for the primary bedroom.

remedies.structural: If redesigning, reserve a stable South-West room for the primary occupants where possible.
remedies.non_structural: Use a solid headboard, reduce clutter and avoid placing the bed directly under a beam.

toilet_direction.label: Toilet / bathroom
toilet_direction.rationale: Traditional guidance generally avoids toilets in the North-East and central zone.

remedies.structural: For major renovations, obtain professional plumbing and structural advice before relocation.
remedies.non_structural: Maintain strong ventilation, fix leaks promptly, keep the door closed and the space dry.

pooja_direction.label: Pooja / meditation room
pooja_direction.rationale: The North-East is traditionally considered suitable for prayer, contemplation and quiet activity.

remedies.structural: When planning interiors, reserve a calm North-East or East niche where practical.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the area clean, quiet and well lit; avoid storing unrelated heavy items there.

living_room_direction.label: Living room
living_room_direction.rationale: Lighter northern and eastern sectors are traditionally preferred for active shared spaces.

remedies.structural: During redesign, improve natural light and circulation in the shared living zone.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the centre open, use balanced seating and reduce visual clutter.

balcony_direction.label: Balcony / open space
balcony_direction.rationale: Open spaces toward North and East are traditionally associated with lightness and openness.

remedies.structural: Avoid structural changes without engineering and society approvals.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the balcony open, bright and free from excessive heavy storage.

staircase_direction.label: Staircase
staircase_direction.rationale: Heavier elements such as staircases are traditionally preferred in southern or western sectors.

remedies.structural: Relocation should only be considered with professional structural review.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the staircase well maintained, illuminated and free from storage obstruction.

children_bedroom_direction.label: Children's bedroom
children_bedroom_direction.rationale: Eastern and northern sectors are traditionally associated with learning and activity.

remedies.structural: Choose an East or North room during future reallocation where possible.
remedies.non_structural: Place the study desk so the child can face East or North and maintain good daylight.

guest_bedroom_direction.label: Guest bedroom
guest_bedroom_direction.rationale: The North-West is traditionally preferred for temporary occupants and guests.

remedies.structural: Reassign rooms rather than alter structure when possible.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the guest room welcoming, airy and minimally cluttered.

dining_direction.label: Dining area
dining_direction.rationale: The dining area is traditionally preferred near the kitchen while keeping the centre unobstructed.

remedies.structural: Keep circulation between kitchen and dining practical during redesign.
remedies.non_structural: Use a clean, well-lit dining area and avoid placing it in a congested central passage.

brahmasthan_direction.label: Brahmasthan / central zone
brahmasthan_direction.rationale: The central zone is traditionally expected to remain relatively open, light and unobstructed.

remedies.structural: Consult an architect before removing walls or structural elements.
remedies.non_structural: Reduce heavy storage and visual congestion in the geometric centre of the property.

underground_tank_direction.label: Underground water tank / borewell
underground_tank_direction.rationale: Traditional Vastu generally favours underground water sources in the North or North-East.

remedies.structural: Any tank relocation requires qualified civil, plumbing and waterproofing advice.
remedies.non_structural: Keep the tank hygienic, sealed and regularly maintained; do not rely on symbolic remedies for safety issues.

overhead_tank_direction.label: Overhead water tank
overhead_tank_direction.rationale: A heavy overhead tank is traditionally preferred in southern or western sectors.

remedies.structural: Relocation or load changes require structural-engineering approval.
remedies.non_structural: Prevent leakage and ensure the supporting structure is professionally inspected.

parking_direction.label: Parking
parking_direction.rationale: North-West and northern sectors are traditionally considered practical for vehicle movement.

remedies.structural: Follow local access, fire and parking regulations before altering the bay.
remedies.non_structural: Keep access unobstructed and avoid long-term clutter around the vehicle.
